A_macro_api.how: Comment- and string-literal-stripped token match on the macro names declared in inc/eshkol/eshkol.h's HEADER ACCESS MACROS block. The macro names are unique identifiers, so the match is exact, not heuristic.
A_macro_api.risk: None. This class is complete by construction.
A_macro_api.what: Uses of the ESHKOL_GET_HEADER macro family.

B_header_type.how: Stripped token match on `eshkol_object_header_t` / `struct eshkol_object_header`, excluding lines already claimed by class A or C.
B_header_type.risk: None for the canonical spelling; aliases are covered by class F.
B_header_type.what: Textual references to the header type itself (declarations, casts, parameters).

C_sizeof_header.how: Stripped regex for `sizeof` applied to any known header type name. These are the sites where the size 8 is load-bearing rather than incidental.
C_sizeof_header.risk: Misses `sizeof *hdr`; that spelling is recovered by the semantic layer (class S2).
C_sizeof_header.what: Header size used as an arithmetic quantity — an offset, an overhead, an allocation adjustment.

D2_ir_field_offset.how: Stripped regex over lib/backend and lib/repl for an LLVM integer constant in -1..-7. `subtype` is at -8, but `flags` is at -7, `ref_count` at -6 and `size` at -4, so every published search for `-8` finds none of these. A migration that changes the header size and diligently fixes every -8 site still leaves this class reading the wrong field of the right header.
D2_ir_field_offset.risk: A small negative constant that is not a header field offset is a false positive. The snippet is recorded for each so the class can be audited by eye; over-reporting here is the safe direction.
D2_ir_field_offset.what: Offsets of individual fields WITHIN the header, emitted as LLVM constants.

D_ir_const_offset.how: Stripped regex over lib/backend and lib/repl for an LLVM integer constant equal to the negated header size — `ConstantInt::get(T, -8)`, `getInt64(-8)`, `CreateConstGEP1_64(..., -8)`. This is the class no grep for the header type finds, because the type name never appears: the compiler emits a raw number. Each such site bakes in TWO facts, the header size and the field offset within it, so a site reading `subtype` emits -8 today and would need -(newsize) + newsubtypeoffset.
D_ir_const_offset.risk: A -8 that means something other than a header offset would be a false positive; the snippet is recorded for every finding so each can be audited. Cross-checked against the `emitted` layer, which counts the offsets that actually reach the IR.
D_ir_const_offset.what: Header offsets baked into emitted LLVM IR as compile-time constants.

E_alloc_with_header.how: Stripped token match on identifiers matching `\w*_with_header\b`. These are the constructor half of the ABI; classes A-D are the reader half. A migration that fixes readers and misses writers produces exactly the silent garbage this inventory exists to prevent.
E_alloc_with_header.risk: None; the naming convention is enforced by class G.
E_alloc_with_header.what: Calls through the `*_with_header` allocator family — the sites that WRITE the layout.

F_parallel_header_decl.how: Parse every `typedef struct { ... } Name;` and `struct Name { ... };` body in the tree and compare its field sequence — types and names in order — against the canonical header's. A structural match under a different name is a second definition of the ABI that no search for the canonical type name will ever find, and that will not be updated when the canonical one is.
F_parallel_header_decl.risk: A struct that coincidentally has the same four fields would be a false positive. That is the correct bias: a coincidence here is worth auditing.
F_parallel_header_decl.what: Struct declarations that structurally duplicate the canonical header under a different name.

G_header_field_write.how: Stripped regex for `<ident>->{subtype,flags,ref_count,size}` where <ident> matches a header-ish name (hdr, header, h, obj_header, ...). Heuristic by design; the semantic layer supersedes it when libclang is available.
G_header_field_write.risk: Both directions. Superseded by class S1 under --clang.
G_header_field_write.what: Direct writes to header fields through a pointer whose name suggests a header.

H_wasm_glue.how: Stripped token match over .js/.mjs/.ts for `*_with_header` and for the header field names appearing as object keys or parameters. The WASM lane reimplements the runtime import surface in JS; an import whose signature mentions a subtype is a layout commitment on the JS side.
H_wasm_glue.risk: Narrow by construction — it cannot see byte offsets computed arithmetically in JS.
H_wasm_glue.what: JavaScript/TypeScript that names a header-aware runtime import or a header field.

I_public_abi.how: Any class A-G finding whose path is an installed header (inc/eshkol/**) is additionally recorded here. These are not merely internal sites: they are commitments to embedders who compiled against them, so they cannot be changed by recompiling this repository alone.
I_public_abi.risk: None; derived from the other classes.
I_public_abi.what: Layout dependence inside a PUBLIC installed header.

J_secondary_prefix_abi.how: Stripped token match on `eshkol_shared_header_t`, plus header-ish field accesses in files that name it but not the object header. Kept as a separate class deliberately: it uses the identical `data - sizeof(header)` idiom and the identical field names (`ref_count`, `flags`), so a migration that pattern-matches on the idiom rather than the type will convert these by accident.
J_secondary_prefix_abi.risk: None; the type name is unique.
J_secondary_prefix_abi.what: The OTHER prefix-header ABI — 24-byte eshkol_shared_header_t on shared/ref-counted allocations.

K_raw_byte_offset.how: Stripped regex for a byte-pointer cast followed by `- 8`, for `*(p - 8)`, and for `ptr - 8`. These sites read as ordinary byte arithmetic; they contain no token that a search for the header type or the accessor macro would match, and they are the sites most likely to survive a migration untouched.
K_raw_byte_offset.risk: Any `- 8` in byte-pointer arithmetic matches. Recorded with snippets for audit.
K_raw_byte_offset.what: Pointer arithmetic that rebuilds the header from raw bytes, naming neither the type nor the macro.

L_layout_in_prose.how: Regex over RAW text — comments deliberately included — for the layout's published spellings: `[header (8 bytes)]`, `8-byte header`, `header is at offset -8`, `[subtype(1)][flags(1)]`. Prose is not compiled, so nothing keeps it true; it goes stale silently and is then read as authoritative. Includes .md, and the published specification pages, because a wrong number in the spec is a wrong number an integrator will implement against.
L_layout_in_prose.risk: None to correctness; this class is a documentation work-list, not a code hazard.
L_layout_in_prose.what: The byte layout restated in comments and documentation.

M_cache_key_without_abi.how: A detector for an ABSENCE: a file that computes a persistent cache key (hashUpdate / xxh3_64bits / a hand-versioned artifact name / addObjectFile) and does NOT mention the ABI fingerprint anywhere. Such a cache will hand back an artifact built against the other layout and the program will run. Absence is the hardest property to watch by hand, which is exactly why it is machined; this class goes empty as the fingerprint is threaded into each key.
M_cache_key_without_abi.risk: Coarse — one finding per file, not per key. It is a work-list of caches to audit, and it is designed to be driven to zero.
M_cache_key_without_abi.what: Persistent artifact caches whose key does not include the object ABI.

R_emitted_ir.how: Compile a corpus with `eshkol-run --dump-ir` and count `getelementptr i8, ptr %x, i64 -8` in the .ll. This is ground truth for the compiler side: it does not depend on any model of the source, so it catches an offset produced by a route no source detector knows about. Reported as a count, not a site list — its purpose is to falsify the claim that the static inventory is complete.
R_emitted_ir.risk: Only covers constructs the corpus exercises. Coverage is the corpus's job, not this detector's.
R_emitted_ir.what: Header offsets that actually reach emitted LLVM IR.

S1_clang_header_member.how: libclang AST walk over the translation units in compile_commands.json; every MEMBER_REF_EXPR whose base expression's canonical type is (pointer to) the header type. Catches accesses through typedefs, `auto`, template parameters, and macro expansions the lexical layer cannot resolve.
S1_clang_header_member.risk: Requires a configured build; skipped without one, and the skip is recorded in the snapshot.
S1_clang_header_member.what: Member accesses whose base resolves to the header type, however spelled.

S2_clang_sizeof.how: libclang: UnaryExprOrTypeTraitExpr whose operand type canonicalizes to the header type.
S2_clang_sizeof.what: sizeof/alignof over the header type, including `sizeof *hdr` and `sizeof(decltype(...))`.

S3_clang_header_cast.how: libclang: any cast expression whose destination type canonicalizes to a pointer to the header type.
S3_clang_header_cast.what: Casts to a header pointer type — the spelling that reconstructs a header from raw bytes.
